title: A proper ideal has a minimal prime over it
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $I\subsetneq\Lambda$ a proper ideal. Then there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\supset I$ of $\Lambda$ that is minimal over $I$: no prime ideal $\mathfrak q'$ with $I\subset\mathfrak q'\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ exists.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), parts (2) (every nonzero ring, here Λ/I, has a maximal ideal) and (4) (a prime containing I contains a prime minimal over I); used as 'Pick a prime q ⊃ h_A such that q is minimal over h_A' in Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem 07GC
